verdict.rationale: Asana's own marketing says users can turn team expertise into custom AI Teammates, and that each agent has its own identity, scoped permissions, audit trail and cost constraints, managed from an admin console. An API endpoint also lists configured agents, so creating and configuring agents inside the product is a first-party capability. The evidence is marketing-level only: there is no step-by-step documentation of the agent-building flow, so the depth of customization is unproven. Missing for 10: documented builder workflow (defining instructions, tools/skills and triggers for a custom agent), confirmation that end users rather than only admins can build agents, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build and configure my own custom AI agent within the product

citations.quote: Turn your team's collective expertise into custom AI Teammates built to handle the complex, coordination-heavy work that slows your team down.
Every agent has an identity, scoped permissions, an audit trail, and cost constraints, with data access, approved actions, and spend all managed from the same console that governs human users.
Returns the compact records of agents (AI Teammates) configured.
